relations.label: father
relations.explain: Children call their father by a word for dad, never by his name.

pronoun.note: Many Bangladeshi families use আপনি with their father (sometimes with both parents); many others use তুমি. Follow your family.

bd.note: আব্বু and আব্বা are very common in Bangladesh; বাবা is understood everywhere.

relations.label: mother
relations.explain: Children call their mother by a word for mum, never by her name.

pronoun.note: Most families use তুমি with their mother; some use আপনি with both parents.

bd.note: আম্মু and আম্মা are very common in Bangladesh; মা is understood everywhere.

relations.label: father's father
relations.explain: Bengali has different words for the grandparents on your father's side and on your mother's side.

pronoun.note: Many grandchildren use তুমি with grandparents; আপনি is never wrong.

bd.note: In these families দাদা means your father's father.

wb.note: In these families দাদা means elder brother, so a grandfather is দাদু.

relations.label: father's older brother
relations.explain: Aunts and uncles are named by the parent they come from, so your father's brother has a word of their own.

pronoun.note: আপনি is the safe choice; many families use তুমি with aunts and uncles they grew up with.

bd.note: With several uncles, the eldest is বড় চাচা, the second মেজো চাচা and the youngest ছোট চাচা.

wb.note: Your father's older brother is জ্যাঠা and his younger brother is কাকা: two different words.

pronoun.note: In many Kolkata families children use তুমি with aunts and uncles.
